response.rationale: R6 uniquely integrates the congenital PFO, severe pulmonary hypertension, right-to-left shunt, and the acyanotic-to-cyanotic transition, forming the complete Eisenmenger syndrome picture. C1 is the closest runner-up because it captures PAH secondary to congenital heart disease but is less syndrome-specific. R5 only documents pulmonary hypertension, R7 only names the PFO, R3 only describes a secondary echocardiographic finding, and R4 is contradicted by pulmonary angiography showing no pulmonary embolism or arteriovenous fistulae.

rejected.why: Describes only the PFO anatomical finding and does not explain the pulmonary hypertension, right-to-left shunt syndrome, or cyanotic progression.
Captures the elevated pulmonary artery pressures but omits the congenital PFO, right-to-left shunt, and cyanosis that define the full clinical syndrome.
Directly contradicted by pulmonary angiography showing no evidence of pulmonary embolism or pulmonary arteriovenous fistulae; hemoptysis and PAH are nonspecific.
Tricuspid regurgitation is secondary to right heart pressure/volume overload and does not explain the PFO-related shunt or cyanosis.
